tools.name: graph_meta
tools.description:
Describe the graph this server reads, without looking up any fact in it.

        Returns the snapshot id and creation time, the schema version with notable schema changes, the node labels (types), the relationship verbs, the contributing sources, and the path templates that graph_path accepts.

tools.name: graph_lookup
tools.description: Start here when a CVE, ATT&CK technique or CWE id appears in your task. Find nodes by exact external id, e.g. CVE-2021-44228, T1059.001, CWE-79. Returns each match with its source (a CVE has a kev node if CISA lists it as exploited, and an nvd node) and a uid for graph_node and graph_neighbors. On t

tools.name: graph_search
tools.description: List nodes whose external id starts with a prefix (e.g. CVE-2024-1, T105). Ids only, not free text. If the answer has truncated: true, pass its next_cursor as cursor to continue; a list without truncated is complete.

tools.name: graph_node
tools.description: One node's properties (long text is clipped). uid comes from graph_lookup or graph_search. On a kev node: date_added, due_date, known_ransomware_use (Known or Unknown; Unknown means not recorded), required_action, vendor_project, product. On an nvd node: description and metadata (cvss_score, affecte

tools.name: graph_neighbors
tools.description: Directly connected nodes with each link's verb, source, confidence and whether it is declared or inferred. Declared and cross-source links come first. If the answer has truncated: true, pass its next_cursor as cursor to continue.

tools.name: graph_path
tools.description: Answer a multi-hop question from an external id in one call instead of several lookups: for a CVE, the attack techniques it enables and the detections and response procedures for them. tools.name: graph_affects
tools.description:

tools.name: graph_exposure
tools.description:
The ATT&CK techniques a posture signal may point to, for a person to read.

tools.name: graph_answer
tools.description: The same answer the Lattice Analyst page gives for ONE CVE: the verdict, the facts behind it (CISA listing and dates, ransomware use as recorded, score, product, fixed versions) and the graph ids it rests on. Written in code from the graph, no model. One exact CVE id per call; no list, search or que

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "graph_lookup" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
